river:泸水.note: On his southern campaign in 225 Zhuge Liang "crossed the Lu in the 5th month and went deep into the barren lands".

river:江（长江）.note: The natural moat between north and south in the Three Kingdoms; Cao Pi of Wei, looking out over it, sighed that "Heaven surely set it here to divide north from south". Red Cliffs, Yiling, Ruxu and other battles were all fought on or beside the river.

river:辽水.note: In 238 Sima Yi crossed the Liao River, feinted at Liaosui and made straight for Xiangping.

river:沔水（汉水）.note: Its upper course runs through Hanzhong and its middle course past Xiangyang and Fancheng, entering the Yangtze at Xiakou. In the autumn rains of 219 the Han River flooded, and Guan Yu drowned Yu Jin's seven armies.

river:湘水.note: In 215 Sun Quan and Liu Bei divided Jing Province between them along the Xiang River.

river:淮水.note: The buffer zone between Wei and Wu; Wei set up military farms on a large scale south and north of the Huai, and the three rebellions in Huainan all took place at Shouchun on its southern bank.

river:嘉陵水.note: Its upper course was called the Gudao River, and the Chencang Road followed its valley.

river:河（黄河）.note: After Wang Jing's river works early in the Eastern Han, the Yellow River ran northeast from Xingyang past Puyang and Dong'e to the sea at Qiansheng, and stayed fairly stable for centuries. In the Guandu campaign it was the natural line across which the two armies faced each other; Baima, Yanjin and Liyang were all crossings on the river.

river:渭水.note: The lifeline of Guanzhong. In 211 Cao Cao crossed the Wei by night and built a sand fort; in 234 Zhuge Liang camped at the Wuzhang Plains and faced Sima Yi across the Wei.

river:漳水.note: It flowed past the north of Ye. In 204 Cao Cao diverted the Zhang to flood Ye.

river:济水.mod: old Ji River (much of the lower Yellow River now follows its course)
river:济水.note: One of the Four Great Rivers; it left the Yellow River at Xingyang, flowed east past Dingtao and the Juye Marsh, and then northeast to the sea.

river:泗水.note: In 198 Cao Cao broke the banks of the Yi and Si to flood Xiapi.

river:易水.note: Gongsun Zan built Yijing beside the Yi River.

river:淯水.note: It flowed past Wan and Xinye into the Han River. In 197, when Zhang Xiu turned on Cao Cao at Wan, Cao Cao fell back to the Yu River.

river:浙江（渐江水）.note: In 196 Sun Ce crossed the Zhe River and defeated Wang Lang.

river:洮水.note: In 255 Jiang Wei routed Wang Jing, the Wei Inspector of Yong Province, at Taoxi.

river:巢湖.note: The Ruxu River flows southeast from Chao Lake into the Yangtze; Wu built Ruxu Fort and the Dongxing dyke at its mouth.

river:居延泽.mod: Ejin Banner, Inner Mongolia (today's Juyan Lake)

river:白水陂.mod: west of Hongze District, Huai'an, Jiangsu
river:白水陂.note: One of the reservoirs Deng Ai built while setting up military farms north of the Huai in Wei's Zhengshi era.

river:云梦泽.note: A vast expanse of lakes and marshes between the Yangtze and the Han, already shrinking by the late Han. When Cao Cao retreated north along the Huarong Road after Red Cliffs, "the road was deep in mud": his route ran through here.

river:大陆泽.mod: Julu and Renze District area, Xingtai, Hebei (silted up)

river:芍陂.mod: south of Shou County, Anhui (Anfeng Pond)
river:芍陂.note: Built by Sunshu Ao of Chu in the Spring and Autumn period and restored by Liu Fu, Inspector of Yang Province, in the late Han; Wei's military farms in Huainan depended on it for irrigation. In 241 the Wu general Quan Cong attacked north and breached Quebei.

river:涡水.note: It flowed past Qiao, Cao Cao's home county; on his southern campaigns Cao Pi often went from Qiao down the Guo into the Huai.

river:沂水.note: In 198 Cao Cao broke the banks of the Yi and Si to flood Xiapi.

river:濡须水.note: The waterway leading east from Chao Lake to the Yangtze. Sun Wu set up Ruxu Fort and built the Dongxing dyke at its mouth; it was a key point north of the river that Wei and Wu fought over.

river:肥水.note: The waterway between Hefei and Shouchun; Wei and Wu attacks and defences in Huainan mostly followed it.

river:西汉水.note: Mount Qi stands on the north bank of the Xihan River.

river:白水.note: Tazhong and Yinping both lie in the Bai River basin, and Baishui Pass guards the point where its lower course leads into Shu.

river:淇水.note: In 204 Cao Cao sank timber piles at the mouth of the Qi to build a weir, diverting the Qi into the Baigou Canal.

canal:汴渠（汳水）.mod: old course of the Bian River
canal:汴渠（汳水）.note: In 69, while taming the Yellow River, Wang Jing also restored the Bian Canal, which ran east from Xingyang past Junyi and Suiyang to join the Si at Pengcheng. It was the main waterway from Luoyang to Xu and Yang provinces; Guandu lay on its upper course.

canal:蒗荡渠（鸿沟）.mod: along the Jialu and Shaying rivers
canal:蒗荡渠（鸿沟）.note: The trunk of the Honggou canal system dug by the state of Wei in the Warring States period, linking the Yellow River and the Huai.

canal:白沟.mod: along the Wei River and the South Canal
canal:白沟.note: In 204, to attack Yuan Shang in the north, Cao Cao sank great timber piles at the point where the Qi entered the Yellow River to build a weir (Fangtou), diverting the Qi northeast into the Baigou Canal to open a supply route. The later Wei River (in Henan and Hebei) and the South Canal follow its line.

canal:利漕渠.note: In 213 Cao Cao dug a canal to lead the Zhang east into the Baigou Canal, so that grain boats could sail from the Baigou Canal straight to Ye.

canal:平虏渠.mod: now lost (roughly in today's Cangzhou, Hebei)
canal:平虏渠.note: In 206, to carry grain for his northern campaign against the Wuhuan, Cao Cao dug a canal from the Hutuo to the Gu River, called the Pinglu Canal.

canal:泉州渠.note: Cao Cao also dug a canal from the mouth of the Ju River into the Lu River, called the Quanzhou Canal, to connect with sea transport.

canal:新河.mod: now lost (roughly in today's Tangshan, Hebei)
canal:新河.note: It ran east from the Quanzhou Canal to the Nuan River, so that grain could be shipped as far as Liaoxi.

canal:破冈渎.mod: now lost (between Jurong and Danyang, Jiangsu)
canal:破冈渎.note: In 245 Sun Quan sent Chen Xun with 30,000 military-farm troops to cut a waterway through Jurong, from Xiaoqi to the western city of Yunyang, so that grain boats between Jianye and Wu and Kuaiji no longer had to go round by the Yangtze.

canal:邗沟.note: Dug by Fuchai, King of Wu, in the Spring and Autumn period to link the Yangtze and the Huai.

canal:吴故水道.note: A waterway from Wu to Jingkou already existed in the Qin and Han; under Sun Wu it was the grain route between Jianye and Wu and Kuaiji.

canal:漕渠.note: Dug under Emperor Wu of the Western Han, it led water from the Wei River east from Chang'an to Huayin.

canal:灵渠.note: Dug under the Qin to link the Xiang and Li rivers.

range:秦岭（南山）.note: The natural barrier between Guanzhong and Hanzhong, crossed by the Ziwu, Tangluo, Baoye and Chencang roads. All five of Zhuge Liang's northern campaigns had to cross the Qinling, and the difficulty of moving grain over them was the greatest constraint on Shu Han's campaigns.

range:巴山.note: The barrier between Hanzhong and Ba–Shu, crossed by the Micang and Jinniu roads.

range:太行山.note: The divide between Hebei and Bing Province. Zhang Yan's Black Mountain army, a Yellow Turban remnant said to number a million, was based in these mountains.

range:陇山.note: The divide between Guanzhong and Longyou, its main routes guarded by the Long and Xiao passes.

range:金微山.note: In 91 Geng Kui and Ren Shang routed the Northern Chanyu here.

range:燕然山.note: In 89, after defeating the Northern Xiongnu, Dou Xian climbed this mountain, and Ban Gu wrote the Inscription for the Feng Sacrifice on Mount Yanran.

range:伏牛山.note: The northern rim of the Nanyang Basin, its eastern outlets guarded by Luyang and She County.

range:大别山.note: The barrier between Wei and Wu in the Jiang–Huai region; Wei's Yiyang and Wu's Qichun faced each other across the mountains.

range:哀牢山.note: In 69 the Ailao kingdom submitted to the Eastern Han, which made its lands into Yongchang Commandery.

range:北邙山.note: The loess ridge north of Luoyang, where many of the Eastern Han emperors were buried; there is a saying "Be born in Suzhou or Hangzhou, be buried at Beimang". In 189 Dong Zhuo met the Young Emperor at Beimang and brought him back.

range:摩天岭.note: The ridge between Wen County in Gansu and Qingchuan and Pingwu in Sichuan; the Yinping Road crossed it going south.

road:褒斜道.note: A plank road built along the valleys of the Ye and Bao rivers, 470 li long, the main route from Guanzhong to Hanzhong. In 228 Zhuge Liang announced that he would come north this way, and in 234 he actually did, camping at the Wuzhang Plains.

road:子午道.mod: south of Xi'an – east of Hanzhong, Shaanxi
road:子午道.note: It left Chang'an due south through the Ziwu Valley and crossed the Qinling to eastern Hanzhong: the shortest route and the most dangerous. In 228 Wei Yan asked to lead 5,000 picked troops this way to surprise Chang'an, but Zhuge Liang judged it too risky and refused; in 230 Cao Zhen also attacked Shu this way and turned back in the rain.

road:傥骆道.note: Its northern entrance, the Luo Valley, was southwest of Zhouzhi and its southern entrance, the Tang Valley, at Yang County; it too was extremely precipitous. Cao Shuang's attack on Shu in 244 and Zhong Hui's march into Hanzhong in 263 both used it.

road:陈仓道.mod: Baoji – Feng County – Lüeyang – Mian County, Shaanxi
road:陈仓道.note: Also called the Gudao Road. It went out through San Pass and south along the Gudao River, curving through eastern Wudu to Hanzhong: long but level. Cao Cao's campaign against Zhang Lu in 215 and Zhuge Liang's siege of Chencang in winter 228 both went this way.

road:祁山道.mod: Mian County, Shaanxi – Li County – Tianshui, Gansu
road:祁山道.note: It went west from Hanzhong and north up the Xihan River valley to Mount Qi, then out to Tianshui. The road was fairly gentle and easy for moving grain, and it allowed the army to link up with the Qiang and Di of Longyou; Zhuge Liang took it on his first and fourth northern campaigns.

road:金牛道.mod: Mian County, Shaanxi – Guangyuan – Jiange – Chengdu, Sichuan
road:金牛道.note: The main route from Hanzhong through Jiange to Chengdu; legend says it was opened when King Hui of Qin tricked Shu with stone oxen that supposedly dropped gold. In 263 Zhong Hui's army marched south along it and was stopped at Jiange.

road:米仓道.note: The route from Hanzhong over the Micang Mountains south to Bazhong. In 215 Zhang Lu fled this way to Bazhong; Zhang He later pushed south to Dangqu and was beaten back by Zhang Fei.

road:阴平道.mod: Wen County, Gansu – Pingwu – Jiangyou, Sichuan
road:阴平道.note: It ran south from Yinping over the Motian Ridge straight to Jiangyou and Mianzhu, mostly through uninhabited, dangerous country that was seldom travelled. In 263 Deng Ai went more than 700 li this way and his surprise attack succeeded.

road:卢龙道.note: In summer 207 floods made the coast road impassable, so Cao Cao took Tian Chou's advice, went out through Lulong Fort and followed an old road disused for two hundred years, "cutting through mountains and filling valleys for more than 500 li", by way of Baitan and Pinggang straight to Liucheng, catching the Wuhuan off guard.

capital:洛阳.mod: east of Luoyang, Henan (Han–Wei Luoyang city site)
capital:洛阳.note: Capital of the Eastern Han. In 190 Dong Zhuo took Emperor Xian west and burned the palaces; Emperor Xian came back to Luoyang briefly in 196 and was soon moved to Xu.

capital:长安.mod: northwest of Xi'an, Shaanxi (Han Chang'an city site)
capital:长安.note: In 190 Dong Zhuo took Emperor Xian west to Chang'an; after Dong Zhuo's death Li Jue and Guo Si controlled the court in turn, until Emperor Xian went east in 195.

capital:安邑.mod: northwest of Xia County, Shanxi (Yuwang City)
capital:安邑.note: Emperor Xian's court in flight on his way east. After crossing the Yellow River in winter 195 he stayed here, "his robes in tatters, with only dates and chestnuts to eat", returning to Luoyang in the 7th month of the next year.

capital:许.mod: Zhangpan Town, Jian'an District, Xuchang, Henan (site of the Han–Wei capital at Xu)
capital:许.note: In 196 Cao Cao brought Emperor Xian here and made it the capital until the abdication of 220; the histories call it the "capital at Xu".

capital:寿春.note: In 197 Yuan Shu proclaimed himself emperor here with the dynastic name Zhong; in 199, abandoned by his followers and kin, he coughed blood and died on his way north.

capital:邺.mod: southwest of Linzhang, Hebei (Ye city site)
capital:邺.note: In 213 Cao Cao, as Duke of Wei, made Ye the capital of the state of Wei and built the Three Terraces; after replacing the Han, Cao Pi moved the capital to Luoyang, but Ye remained one of the Five Capitals of Wei.

capital:洛阳#2.mod: east of Luoyang, Henan (Han–Wei Luoyang city site)
capital:洛阳#2.note: In 220 Cao Pi replaced the Han, made Luoyang his capital and rebuilt the palaces; Emperor Ming of Wei built lavishly, raising the Zhaoyang Hall and the Taiji Hall.

capital:成都.note: Capital of Shu Han (221–263). Zhuge Liang used Shu brocade to fund the army and set up a Brocade Office southwest of the city, which is why Chengdu is also called the Brocade Office City.

capital:武昌.note: In 221 Sun Quan moved here from Gong'an, and after proclaiming himself emperor in 229 moved east to Jianye; in 265 Sun Hao moved the capital here again for a year, when a children's rhyme ran "Better drink Jianye water than eat Wuchang fish".

capital:建业.note: Capital of Wu (229–280, with a brief move to Wuchang). Sun Quan built Stone City and the Jianye Palace, and dug the Pogang Canal to reach Wu and Kuaiji.

capital:襄平.note: In 237 Gongsun Yuan made himself King of Yan with Xiangping as his capital; the next year Sima Yi took it.

capital:洛阳#3.mod: east of Luoyang, Henan (Han–Wei Luoyang city site)
capital:洛阳#3.note: Sima Yan accepted the abdication in 265 and kept Luoyang as his capital.

battle:稽落山之战.sides: Han and the Southern Xiongnu defeated the Northern Xiongnu
battle:稽落山之战.cmd: Dou Xian and Geng Bing vs. the Northern Chanyu
battle:稽落山之战.note: Dou Xian and Geng Bing led Han troops and Southern Xiongnu cavalry beyond the frontier, routed the Northern Chanyu and took the surrender of more than 200,000 people; Dou Xian climbed the Yanran Mountains and had Ban Gu compose an inscription carved in the rock to record his victory before returning.

battle:金微山之战.cmd: Geng Kui and Ren Shang vs. the Northern Chanyu
battle:金微山之战.note: Geng Kui and Ren Shang went more than 5,000 li beyond the Juyan frontier and routed the Northern Chanyu in the Jinwei Mountains; the main body of the Northern Xiongnu moved west, and all the land north of the Gobi passed to the Xianbei.

battle:焉耆之战.sides: Han (with troops from the states of the Western Regions) defeated Karasahr
battle:焉耆之战.cmd: Ban Chao vs. Guang, King of Karasahr
battle:焉耆之战.note: Ban Chao raised more than 70,000 troops from eight states including Kucha and Shanshan to attack Karasahr, beheaded the kings of Karasahr and Weili and sent their heads to the capital; the fifty-odd states of the Western Regions all sent hostages and submitted.

battle:逢义山之战.cmd: Duan Jiong vs. the Xianlian Qiang
battle:逢义山之战.note: Duan Jiong broke the Xianlian Qiang at Mount Fengyi with three ranks of long spears flanked by strong crossbows. In the next two years he fought 180 battles large and small and pacified the Eastern Qiang completely, but at a cost of over four billion cash that left Liang Province gravely weakened.

battle:三道出塞.mod: beyond the frontier, central Inner Mongolia
battle:三道出塞.cmd: Tanshihuai vs. Xia Yu, Tian Yan and Zang Min
battle:三道出塞.note: Emperor Ling sent three generals, each with 10,000 horsemen, out through Gaoliu, Yunzhong and Yanmen. They pushed more than 2,000 li beyond the frontier, where Tanshihuai met each column separately; they lost their tallies, passes and baggage, each general escaped with a few dozen riders, and seven or eight in ten of their men died.

battle:长社之战.cmd: Huangfu Song, Zhu Jun and Cao Cao vs. Bo Cai
battle:长社之战.note: Bo Cai besieged Huangfu Song at Changshe, camping among the grass; Huangfu Song set fires on a windy night and, joined by the newly arrived Chief Commandant of Cavalry Cao Cao, attacked, beheading tens of thousands. The Yingchuan Yellow Turbans scattered.

battle:宛城之围.cmd: Zhu Jun, Qin Jie and Sun Jian vs. Zhang Mancheng, Zhao Hong and Han Zhong
battle:宛城之围.note: Zhang Mancheng of the Nanyang Yellow Turbans killed the Administrator Chu Gong and held Wan for more than a hundred days. After Qin Jie beheaded Zhang Mancheng, Zhao Hong and then Han Zhong held the city; Zhu Jun besieged it for several months before it fell, with Sun Jian first over the wall.

battle:广宗之战.note: Lu Zhi first besieged Guangzong but was falsely accused by eunuchs and imprisoned; Dong Zhuo replaced him and achieved nothing. When Huangfu Song arrived he made a night attack while the Yellow Turbans were off guard, beheaded Zhang Liang, took 30,000 heads, and 50,000 more drowned in the river. Zhang Jue had already died of illness; his coffin was opened and his corpse mutilated.

battle:下曲阳之战.cmd: Huangfu Song and Guo Dian vs. Zhang Bao
battle:下曲阳之战.note: Following up his victory, Huangfu Song attacked Xiaquyang, beheaded Zhang Bao, the "General of Earth", killed or captured more than 100,000 and piled their bodies into a mound south of the city. With this the main Yellow Turban force was put down.

battle:美阳之战.sides: Han defeated the Liang Province rebels
battle:美阳之战.cmd: Zhang Wen and Dong Zhuo vs. Bian Zhang and Han Sui
battle:美阳之战.note: Bian Zhang and Han Sui led tens of thousands of Qiang and Hu horsemen into the Three Adjuncts, and the Excellency of Works Zhang Wen camped at Meiyang with the armies. One night a meteor lit up the camp; the rebels took it as an ill omen and prepared to withdraw, and Dong Zhuo seized the chance to defeat them. Sun Jian was also with Zhang Wen's army at this time.

battle:陈仓之围.mod: east of Chencang District, Baoji, Shaanxi
battle:陈仓之围.sides: Han defeated the Liang Province rebels
battle:陈仓之围.cmd: Huangfu Song and Dong Zhuo vs. Wang Guo and Han Sui
battle:陈仓之围.note: Wang Guo, Han Sui and others besieged Chencang for more than eighty days without taking it. Huangfu Song rejected Dong Zhuo's call for an immediate relief attack and waited until the besiegers were exhausted, then pursued and routed them. Wang Guo was deposed by Han Sui and the others, and the Liang Province rebels fell to quarrelling.

battle:汴水之战.cmd: Xu Rong vs. Cao Cao and Wei Zi
battle:汴水之战.note: While the eastern generals sat at Suanzao, Cao Cao alone led his troops west. At the Bian River near Xingyang he met Dong Zhuo's officer Xu Rong and fought all day, losing many men; Cao Cao was hit by a stray arrow and his horse was wounded, and he escaped only because Cao Hong gave him his own horse.

battle:河阳津之战.note: Wang Kuang camped at Heyang Ford intending to cross the Yellow River. Dong Zhuo pretended to cross at Pingyin while secretly sending picked troops across to the north at Xiaoping Ford to get behind him, and crushed Wang Kuang's army, almost to the last man.

battle:梁东之战.note: Sun Jian advanced from Luyang to camp east of Liang County and was defeated by Xu Rong. His officer Zu Mao put on Sun Jian's red woollen headscarf to draw off the pursuers, so that Sun Jian escaped, gathered his scattered men and advanced again.

battle:阳人之战.cmd: Sun Jian vs. Hu Zhen and Lü Bu
battle:阳人之战.note: Dong Zhuo sent Hu Zhen and Lü Bu to attack Sun Jian at Yangren; the two generals were at odds, and their army panicked in the night. Sun Jian sallied out, routed them and beheaded their commander Hua Xiong. The Romance's story of Guan Yu "slaying Hua Xiong while the wine was still warm" is a novelist's invention.

battle:襄阳之战.note: Yuan Shu sent Sun Jian south against Liu Biao. Sun Jian defeated Huang Zu between Fan and Deng and besieged Xiangyang, but while riding alone on Mount Xian he was shot dead by Huang Zu's soldiers, aged thirty-seven.

battle:东光之战.sides: Gongsun Zan defeated the Qing Province Yellow Turbans
battle:东光之战.cmd: Gongsun Zan vs. the Qing Province Yellow Turbans
battle:东光之战.note: Three hundred thousand Yellow Turbans of Qing and Xu provinces entered Bohai, hoping to join the Black Mountain army. Gongsun Zan met them south of Dongguang with 20,000 foot and horse, beheaded 30,000, and wiped out tens of thousands more in pursuit at the Yellow River, making his name feared.

battle:界桥之战.cmd: Qu Yi and Yuan Shao vs. Gongsun Zan
battle:界桥之战.note: Gongsun Zan drew up 30,000 infantry in a square with 10,000 horsemen on the wings. Yuan Shao had Qu Yi lead 800 vanguard troops, with a thousand strong crossbows hidden under shields, who held their fire until the White Horse Volunteers were almost upon them and then loosed together, routing them and killing Gongsun Zan's Inspector of Ji Province, Yan Gang. South of Jieqiao Yuan Shao was briefly surrounded by Gongsun Zan's remaining cavalry; he threw his helmet to the ground and fought desperately.

battle:寿张之战.sides: Cao Cao defeated the Qing Province Yellow Turbans
battle:寿张之战.cmd: Cao Cao and Bao Xin vs. the Qing Province Yellow Turbans
battle:寿张之战.note: Cao Cao and Bao Xin fought the Yellow Turbans east of Shouzhang, where Bao Xin died fighting hard. Cao Cao fought day and night with surprise troops and pursued the Yellow Turbans to Jibei; in winter he took the surrender of more than 300,000 fighters and picked the best of them as the "Qing Province troops", laying the foundation of his power.

battle:长安之战.sides: Li Jue and Guo Si defeated Lü Bu and Wang Yun
battle:长安之战.cmd: Li Jue, Guo Si and Fan Chou vs. Lü Bu
battle:长安之战.note: After Dong Zhuo's death Wang Yun refused to pardon his Liang Province followers; Jia Xu urged Li Jue and the others to "lead the troops west". Gathering men along the way until they numbered over 100,000, they besieged Chang'an for eight days and took it; Lü Bu was defeated and fled, Wang Yun was killed, and more than 10,000 officials and townspeople died.

battle:匡亭之战.cmd: Cao Cao vs. Yuan Shu and Liu Xiang
battle:匡亭之战.note: Yuan Shu led his troops into Chenliu and camped at Fengqiu, allying with Yufuluo of the Southern Xiongnu and remnants of the Black Mountains. Cao Cao routed his general Liu Xiang at Kuangting and pursued to Xiangyi and Ningling, and Yuan Shu fled all the way south to Jiujiang.

battle:彭城之战.note: On his eastern campaign Cao Cao took more than ten cities and routed Tao Qian at Pengcheng, killing tens of thousands, so that "the Si River ceased to flow"; Tao Qian fell back to hold Tan. Cao Cao's army massacred widely wherever it went, and many scholars and common people of Xu Province fled south to Jiangdong.

battle:龙凑之战.note: Gongsun Zan attacked Yuan Shao to the south at Longcou and came back badly beaten; after this he no longer dared to advance south lightly and turned to consolidating You Province.

battle:居庸之战.note: Liu Yu attacked Gongsun Zan at Ji with 100,000 men but forbade them to burn homes or harm the innocent; a few hundred of Gongsun Zan's picked men set fires and scattered them instead. Liu Yu fled north to Juyong County and was captured, and was later executed on the charge of plotting with Yuan Shao to make himself emperor.

battle:郯东之战.sides: Cao Cao defeated Tao Qian and Liu Bei
battle:郯东之战.cmd: Cao Cao vs. Cao Bao and Liu Bei
battle:郯东之战.note: On his second attack on Xu Province Cao Cao took the counties of Langya and Donghai and routed Tao Qian's officer Cao Bao and Liu Bei east of Tan. Tao Qian, terrified, was about to flee to Danyang when Lü Bu seized Yan Province, and Cao Cao hurried back.

battle:濮阳之战.cmd: Cao Cao vs. Lü Bu and Chen Gong
battle:濮阳之战.note: Cao Cao attacked Lü Bu at Puyang; after entering by the east gate he ran into an ambush with fire, burned the palm of his left hand, fell from his horse and was nearly captured. The two sides then faced each other for more than a hundred days, until a locust plague and famine made both withdraw.

battle:定陶巨野之战.cmd: Cao Cao vs. Lü Bu and Chen Gong
battle:定陶巨野之战.note: Cao Cao first beheaded Lü Bu's officers Xue Lan and Li Feng at Juye, then crushed Lü Bu and Chen Gong with an ambush at Dingtao. Lü Bu fled east to Liu Bei in Xu Province, and Cao Cao gradually recovered Yan Province.

battle:雍丘之战.note: Zhang Miao's brother Zhang Chao held Yongqiu. Cao Cao besieged it for several months; in the 12th month the city fell, Zhang Chao killed himself, and Cao Cao wiped out the three branches of Zhang Miao's family. Zhang Miao himself was killed by his own men on his way to ask Yuan Shu for help.

battle:曹阳之战.sides: Li Jue and Guo Si defeated Yang Feng and Dong Cheng
battle:曹阳之战.cmd: Li Jue, Guo Si and Zhang Ji vs. Yang Feng and Dong Cheng
battle:曹阳之战.note: When Emperor Xian had come east as far as Hongnong, Li Jue and Guo Si thought better of letting him go and pursued him; they routed his escort at Dongjian, killing countless officials and soldiers, and the palace women and imperial goods were all lost. Emperor Xian crossed the Yellow River by night and took up residence at Anyi.

battle:牛渚之战.cmd: Sun Ce vs. Zhang Ying and Fan Neng
battle:牛渚之战.note: Sun Ce set out east with a thousand-odd men borrowed from Yuan Shu; by the time he reached Liyang he had five or six thousand, and he crossed the Yangtze and took Liu Yao's camp at Niuzhu with all its stores of grain and equipment; in the course of the campaign he fought Taishi Ci hand to hand at Shenting. He went on to defeat Ze Rong and Xue Li, and Liu Yao abandoned Qu'e and fled to Yuzhang.

battle:鲍丘之战.sides: Yuan Shao and Liu He defeated Gongsun Zan
battle:鲍丘之战.cmd: Qu Yi, Xianyu Fu, Yan Rou and Liu He vs. Gongsun Zan
battle:鲍丘之战.note: Xianyu Fu, one of Liu Yu's former officers, made Yan Rou Major over the Wuhuan and brought in more than 7,000 Wuhuan and Xianbei horsemen. Joining Yuan Shao's general Qu Yi and Liu Yu's son Liu He, 100,000 strong, they routed Gongsun Zan at Baoqiu, beheading more than 20,000, and the commanderies of You Province all killed the officials Gongsun Zan had installed.

battle:吕布袭下邳.sides: Lü Bu defeated Liu Bei (Zhang Fei)
battle:吕布袭下邳.note: While Liu Bei faced Yuan Shu at Xuyi and Huaiyin he left Zhang Fei to hold Xiapi. Zhang Fei quarrelled with Cao Bao, Chancellor of Xiapi, and killed him; in the confusion in the city Lü Bu made a night attack, took the city and captured Liu Bei's wife and children. Liu Bei could not get back in time, later submitted to Lü Bu and went back to camp at Xiaopei.

battle:固陵之战.mod: west of Xiaoshan District, Hangzhou, Zhejiang
battle:固陵之战.note: Sun Ce crossed the Zhe River to attack Kuaiji, and Wang Lang held Guling against him. Following his uncle Sun Jing's plan, Sun Ce sent a detachment by night through Zhadu to surprise the Gaoqian camp; Wang Lang was routed, fled by sea south to Dongye, and surrendered the next year.

battle:宛城之战.cmd: Zhang Xiu and Jia Xu vs. Cao Cao
battle:宛城之战.note: Zhang Xiu surrendered to Cao Cao with all his men, but Cao Cao took Zhang Ji's widow into his household; Zhang Xiu, resentful, followed Jia Xu's plan and launched a surprise attack on Cao Cao's camp. Cao Cao's eldest son Cao Ang gave his father his horse and was killed, Dian Wei died holding the camp gate, and Cao Cao, hit in the right arm by a stray arrow, fled back to Wuyin.

battle:蕲阳之战.cmd: Cao Cao vs. Qiao Rui, Li Feng, Liang Gang and Yue Jiu
battle:蕲阳之战.note: Yuan Shu was attacking Chen Kingdom when he heard Cao Cao was coming east; he abandoned his army and fled across the Huai, leaving Qiao Rui and three other generals to hold off Cao Cao at Qiyang, where all were killed. Yuan Shu was gravely weakened, and Huainan was then struck by drought and famine.

battle:安众之战.sides: Cao Cao defeated Zhang Xiu and Liu Biao
battle:安众之战.note: Cao Cao was besieging Zhang Xiu at Rang when he heard that Yuan Shao meant to strike at Xu, and withdrew. Zhang Xiu and Liu Biao combined to cut off his retreat at Anzhong; Cao Cao cut a path through the hills by night, hid troops there, and caught them front and rear, routing them.

battle:下邳之战.cmd: Cao Cao and Liu Bei vs. Lü Bu, Chen Gong and Gao Shun
battle:下邳之战.note: Cao Cao massacred Pengcheng and besieged Lü Bu at Xiapi for three months, following the plans of Xun You and Guo Jia to breach the Yi and Si rivers and flood the city. Lü Bu's officers Hou Cheng, Song Xian and Wei Xu tied up Chen Gong and surrendered, and Lü Bu asked to surrender at the White Gate Tower; Cao Cao listened to Liu Bei's words, "Has my lord not seen how Lü Bu served Ding Jianyang and Grand Preceptor Dong?", and had him strangled.

battle:易京之战.note: Yuan Shao besieged Yijing for a year. Gongsun Zan sent to Zhang Yan of the Black Mountains for help, arranging a fire signal, but the letter fell into Yuan Shao's hands. Yuan Shao dug tunnels under the towers and burned their pillars, the towers collapsed and the city fell; Gongsun Zan killed his wife and children and then burned himself to death.

battle:射犬之战.cmd: Shi Huan and Cao Ren vs. Sui Gu
battle:射犬之战.note: After Zhang Yang's death his officer Sui Gu planned to go over to Yuan Shao and camped at Shequan; Cao Cao sent Shi Huan and Cao Ren across the Yellow River to attack and behead him. Henei passed to Cao Cao, who then advanced to Liyang and Guandu.

battle:皖城之战.cmd: Sun Ce and Zhou Yu vs. Liu Xun
battle:皖城之战.note: Feigning friendship, Sun Ce persuaded Liu Xun, Administrator of Lujiang, to attack Shangliao, then took the undefended Wancheng, gaining more than 30,000 of Yuan Shu's retainers and craftsmen; Sun Ce married the elder Qiao and Zhou Yu the younger.

battle:沙羡之战.cmd: Sun Ce vs. Huang Zu, Liu Hu and Han Xi
battle:沙羡之战.note: Sun Ce attacked Huang Zu at Shayi to the west; Liu Biao sent his nephew Liu Hu and Han Xi of Nanyang with 5,000 long-spear troops to help. Sun Ce routed them, beheaded Han Xi and took 6,000 boats, and Huang Zu escaped alone.

battle:小沛之战.note: After the plot of the Edict in the Girdle was discovered, Cao Cao marched in person against Liu Bei despite the threat from Yuan Shao. Liu Bei was defeated and fled north to Yuan Tan and Yuan Shao, and his wife and children were captured; Guan Yu, holding Xiapi, was captured and went over to Cao Cao for a time.

battle:白马之战.cmd: Cao Cao, Guan Yu and Zhang Liao vs. Yan Liang
battle:白马之战.note: Yuan Shao sent Yan Liang to attack Baima. On Xun You's advice Cao Cao feinted towards Yanjin and then turned back to strike Baima; Guan Yu, seeing Yan Liang's banner and canopy, galloped at him through ten thousand men, stabbed him and came back with his head. The Romance's "passing five passes and slaying six generals" is fiction.

battle:延津之战.cmd: Cao Cao vs. Wen Chou and Liu Bei
battle:延津之战.note: Cao Cao moved his baggage from Baima west along the Yellow River; Yuan Shao's army pursued to south of Yanjin. Cao Cao left the baggage on the road as bait, and while the Yuan troops scrambled for it he attacked with fewer than 600 horsemen and killed Wen Chou. The loss of two famous generals in a row badly shook Yuan Shao's army.

battle:官渡之战.note: Yuan Shao marched south with more than 100,000 men and faced Cao Cao at Guandu for months, the two sides building earth mounds and digging tunnels against each other. Cao Cao's food ran out and he almost withdrew to Xu, but Xun Yu urged him to hold on. Xu You defected from Yuan Shao and proposed the raid on Wuchao, and Yuan Shao's army collapsed. The battle laid the foundation for Cao Cao's unification of the north.

battle:乌巢之战.note: Cao Cao personally led 5,000 foot and horse under Yuan Shao's banners, marching silently by night, and attacked the more than 10,000 carts of grain guarded by Chunyu Qiong, burning all of it. Yuan Shao's detachment sent against the main camp at Guandu failed to take it, Zhang He and Gao Lan surrendered, and the Yuan army fell apart.

battle:仓亭之战.note: Yuan Shao gathered his scattered troops at Cangting, and Cao Cao defeated him again; Yuan Shao fell ill and died in the 5th month of the next year. Cheng Yu's "ambush on ten sides" in the Romance is largely fiction.

battle:汝南之战.cmd: Cao Cao vs. Liu Bei and Gong Du
battle:汝南之战.note: In Runan Liu Bei joined Gong Du and other Yellow Turban remnants to raid behind Xu, killing Cao Cao's general Cai Yang; Cao Cao marched south in person, and Liu Bei fled to Liu Biao in Jing Province. The Romance's "Guan Yu slays Cai Yang" is adapted from this.

battle:博望之战.sides: Liu Bei defeated Xiahou Dun and Yu Jin
battle:博望之战.cmd: Liu Bei vs. Xiahou Dun, Yu Jin and Li Dian
battle:博望之战.note: Liu Biao sent Liu Bei north as far as She, and Cao Cao sent Xiahou Dun, Yu Jin and others against him. One day Liu Bei burned his camp and pretended to flee; Xiahou Dun pursued into an ambush and was beaten, escaping only when Li Dian came to his rescue. The Romance credits the victory to Zhuge Liang in his first campaign, but at that time Zhuge Liang had not yet entered Liu Bei's service.

battle:黎阳之战.sides: Cao Cao defeated Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang
battle:黎阳之战.cmd: Cao Cao vs. Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang
battle:黎阳之战.note: After Yuan Shao's death Cao Cao crossed north and attacked Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang at Liyang for half a year, and the two Yuans fell back to Ye; on Guo Jia's advice Cao Cao pulled back for a while to let the brothers fight each other.

battle:邺城之战.sides: Cao Cao defeated Yuan Shang (Shen Pei)
battle:邺城之战.cmd: Cao Cao vs. Shen Pei and Yuan Shang
battle:邺城之战.note: Cao Cao besieged Ye while Yuan Shang was attacking Yuan Tan, digging a trench forty li around and flooding the city with the Zhang River; more than half the people inside starved to death. Yuan Shang came back to relieve it and was crushed; in the 8th month Shen Pei's nephew opened a gate to Cao Cao's troops, and Shen Pei was captured and died unbowed.

battle:南皮之战.note: Cao Cao attacked Yuan Tan at Nanpi. The first fighting went badly, so Cao Cao beat the war drums himself to drive his men on; the city fell, Yuan Tan was beheaded with his wife and children, and Ji Province was pacified.

battle:壶关之战.cmd: Cao Cao, Yue Jin and Li Dian vs. Gao Gan
battle:壶关之战.note: Gao Gan rebelled again and held Hu Pass; Cao Cao besieged it for three months before taking it. Gao Gan fled south towards Jing Province and was beheaded on the way by Wang Yan, Chief Commandant of Shangluo, and Bing Province was pacified.

battle:白狼山之战.sides: Cao Cao defeated the Wuhuan and the Yuan brothers
battle:白狼山之战.cmd: Zhang Liao and Cao Cao vs. Tadun, Yuan Shang and Yuan Xi
battle:白狼山之战.note: Cao Cao went out through Lulong Fort and marched more than 500 li through uninhabited country; at White Wolf Mountain his vanguard ran suddenly into tens of thousands of Wuhuan horsemen. Seeing from a height that the enemy's ranks were in disorder, Cao Cao sent Zhang Liao ahead to charge, killing Tadun and the named kings below him; more than 200,000 Hu and Han surrendered.

battle:江夏之战.cmd: Sun Quan, Lü Meng, Ling Tong and Dong Xi vs. Huang Zu
battle:江夏之战.note: On Sun Quan's third campaign west against Jiangxia, Huang Zu blocked the mouth of the Mian with two covered assault ships; Dong Xi and Ling Tong led a hundred men ready to die, in double armour, who cut the great cables, Lü Meng beheaded Huang Zu's commander Chen Jiu, and the city fell. Huang Zu was beheaded by the horseman Feng Ze, and Sun Quan at last avenged his father.

battle:长坂之战.cmd: Cao Chun (Tiger and Leopard Cavalry) vs. Liu Bei, Zhang Fei and Zhao Yun
battle:长坂之战.note: Liu Bei was retreating south with more than 100,000 people and several thousand carts, covering only ten-odd li a day; Cao Cao personally led 5,000 elite cavalry over 300 li in a day and a night and caught him at Changban near Dangyang. Liu Bei abandoned his wife and children and fled with a few dozen horsemen; Zhang Fei held the river, broke the bridge and faced the enemy with glaring eyes and levelled spear, and Zhao Yun saved the infant Liu Shan in his arms and protected Lady Gan.

battle:赤壁之战.sides: Sun Quan and Liu Bei defeated Cao Cao
battle:赤壁之战.cmd: Zhou Yu, Cheng Pu and Liu Bei vs. Cao Cao
battle:赤壁之战.note: Cao Cao, claiming 800,000 men (Zhou Yu estimated the troops from the north at no more than 150,000–160,000, plus 70,000–80,000 newly surrendered Jing Province troops), came down the Yangtze and met the Sun–Liu allies at Red Cliffs; beaten in the first clash, he withdrew to camp at Wulin on the north bank. Huang Gai proposed a fire attack: several dozen assault ships and warships were loaded with brushwood soaked in oil and sent in under a pretended surrender. With a strong southeast wind blowing, the fire spread to the camps on the north bank; Cao Cao's army was routed, then struck by an epidemic, and Cao Cao escaped on foot along the Huarong Road.

battle:合肥之战.note: After Red Cliffs Sun Quan led 100,000 men in person and besieged Hefei for more than a hundred days; Jiang Ji, Attendant Officer of Yang Province, spread word that 40,000 reinforcements were coming, and Sun Quan burned his camp and withdrew.

battle:江陵之战.cmd: Zhou Yu, Gan Ning and Liu Bei vs. Cao Ren
battle:江陵之战.note: Zhou Yu and Cheng Pu besieged Jiangling. Gan Ning, sent separately to take Yiling, was surrounded there, and Zhou Yu went to his rescue and broke the siege; directing the fighting in person, Zhou Yu was hit in the right side by a stray arrow but still rallied his troops. After more than a year Cao Ren abandoned the city and withdrew north, and Zhou Yu became Administrator of Nan Commandery.

battle:潼关之战.sides: Cao Cao defeated Ma Chao and Han Sui
battle:潼关之战.cmd: Cao Cao vs. Ma Chao and Han Sui
battle:潼关之战.note: Cao Cao reached Tong Pass and faced Ma Chao across it, while secretly sending Xu Huang and Zhu Ling west across the Yellow River at Puban Ford. As Cao Cao crossed with the rearguard, Ma Chao attacked with more than 10,000 horsemen; Xu Chu helped Cao Cao into a boat, and Ding Fei let loose oxen and horses to distract the enemy, so that he got across. The Romance's "cutting his beard and throwing off his robe" is embroidered from this.

battle:渭南之战.sides: Cao Cao defeated Ma Chao and Han Sui
battle:渭南之战.cmd: Cao Cao vs. Ma Chao and Han Sui
battle:渭南之战.note: Cao Cao crossed the Wei River by night and built a sand fort for his camp; Ma Chao attacked repeatedly but could not dislodge him, and asked for a division of territory in return for peace. Using Jia Xu's plan, Cao Cao chatted about old times with Han Sui in front of the lines and deliberately sent him a letter full of erasures, making Ma Chao suspect Han Sui. In the 9th month they met in a set battle: Cao Cao first sent light troops to provoke the enemy, then struck from both sides with his tiger cavalry, routing the coalition of the ten Guanzhong warlords.

battle:濡须口之战.cmd: Cao Cao vs. Sun Quan and Lü Meng
battle:濡须口之战.note: Cao Cao, claiming 400,000 men, attacked Ruxu and took Sun Quan's camp west of the Yangtze. After facing each other for more than a month, seeing the good order of Sun Quan's ships, arms and troops, he sighed "A son should be like Sun Zhongmou" and led his army back north. Sun Quan had built Ruxu Fort beforehand on Lü Meng's advice, and it became Wu's key stronghold north of the Yangtze.

battle:冀城之战.sides: Ma Chao defeated Wei Kang; the next year Yang Fu and others drove Ma Chao out
battle:冀城之战.cmd: Ma Chao vs. Wei Kang, Yang Fu and Jiang Xu
battle:冀城之战.note: Ma Chao attacked Jicheng with Qiang and Hu troops; Wei Kang, Inspector of Liang Province, held out for eight months, surrendered when no relief came, and was killed by Ma Chao. That autumn the Army Adviser Yang Fu and Jiang Xu rose at Lucheng; they lured Ma Chao out of Jicheng, shut the gates behind him and killed his wife and children. Ma Chao attacked Licheng and killed Jiang Xu's mother; defeated by Xiahou Yuan in 214, he went south to Zhang Lu.

battle:雒城之战.sides: Liu Bei defeated Liu Zhang (Liu Xun)
battle:雒城之战.cmd: Liu Bei and Pang Tong vs. Liu Xun and Zhang Ren
battle:雒城之战.note: Liu Bei came south from Jiameng, beheaded Yang Huai and Gao Pei to take Fu, took the surrender of Li Yan at Mianzhu and besieged Luocheng. Liu Zhang's son Liu Xun held out for nearly a year; Pang Tong was killed by a stray arrow while leading an assault, and Zhang Ren was captured in a sortie and died refusing to surrender. The city fell in summer 214, and Liu Bei joined Zhuge Liang, Zhang Fei and Zhao Yun to besiege Chengdu.

battle:皖城之战（214）.sides: Sun Quan defeated Cao Cao (Zhu Guang)
battle:皖城之战（214）.cmd: Lü Meng and Gan Ning vs. Zhu Guang
battle:皖城之战（214）.note: Cao Cao had made Zhu Guang Administrator of Lujiang, stationed at Wan, where he opened up rice fields on a large scale. Lü Meng urged Sun Quan to take it quickly; with Gan Ning commanding the assault and Lü Meng beating the war drums himself, the city fell between dawn and breakfast time, and Zhu Guang and tens of thousands of men and women were captured.

battle:枹罕之战.sides: Cao Cao (Xiahou Yuan) defeated Song Jian
battle:枹罕之战.note: Xiahou Yuan besieged Fuhan for over a month; when it fell he beheaded Song Jian and his chancellor and the officials under him, ending thirty years of independent rule. He also sent Zhang He across the Yellow River into Lesser Huangzhong, and the Qiang of Hexi all submitted.

battle:阳平关之战.sides: Cao Cao defeated Zhang Wei (Zhang Lu)
battle:阳平关之战.cmd: Cao Cao vs. Zhang Wei and Yang Ang
battle:阳平关之战.note: Cao Cao marched in person against Zhang Lu. Zhang Wei held Yangping Pass, building walls along the hills for more than ten li; Cao Cao could not take it and pretended to withdraw, and when Zhang Wei's guard relaxed Cao Cao's troops attacked by night (by another account they strayed into the enemy camp by mistake) and broke through. Zhang Lu sealed his treasuries and fled to Bazhong, surrendering in the 11th month; he was made General Who Guards the South and Marquis of Langzhong.

battle:宕渠之战.note: Zhang He came south into Baxi intending to move its people to Hanzhong, and advanced to Dangqu, Mengtou and Dangshi. Zhang Fei with more than 10,000 picked troops intercepted him by another road; Zhang He abandoned his horses, climbed into the hills and escaped back to Nanzheng by side paths with ten-odd of his men, and Baxi was secure.

battle:逍遥津之战.sides: Cao Cao (Zhang Liao) defeated Sun Quan
battle:逍遥津之战.cmd: Zhang Liao, Li Dian and Yue Jin vs. Sun Quan
battle:逍遥津之战.note: Sun Quan attacked Hefei with 100,000 men; there were only 7,000 in the city. Following Cao Cao's sealed instructions, Zhang Liao recruited 800 men ready to die, and at dawn, in armour and with halberd in hand, charged the enemy lines right up to Sun Quan's banner. Sun Quan besieged the city for more than ten days without success; as he withdrew, Zhang Liao caught him north of Xiaoyao Ford, and he escaped only thanks to Ling Tong's desperate fighting and his horse's leap across the broken bridge.

battle:濡须之战（217）.sides: Stalemate; Sun Quan sued for peace
battle:濡须之战（217）.cmd: Cao Cao vs. Sun Quan, Lü Meng and Gan Ning
battle:濡须之战（217）.note: Cao Cao attacked Sun Quan again at Ruxu; Gan Ning led a hundred-odd men in a night raid on Cao Cao's camp and came back with several dozen heads. Unable to match Cao Cao's strength, Sun Quan sent envoys to offer submission and make peace, and Cao Cao withdrew, leaving Xiahou Dun, Cao Ren and Zhang Liao stationed at Juchao.

battle:定军山之战.cmd: Huang Zhong and Fa Zheng vs. Xiahou Yuan
battle:定军山之战.note: Liu Bei crossed the Mian River south from Yangping Pass, advanced along the hills and camped at Mount Dingjun. Xiahou Yuan came to contest it; Fa Zheng urged attacking from the heights, and Huang Zhong drove forward amid the thunder of drums and gongs and cut down Xiahou Yuan in the fighting. The Cao army fell apart.

battle:汉水之战.cmd: Zhao Yun and Huang Zhong vs. Cao Cao
battle:汉水之战.note: Cao Cao came to Hanzhong in person and moved grain below the northern hills. Huang Zhong went to seize it and was surrounded; Zhao Yun came to his support and was chased back to his camp. He opened the gates, lowered the flags and silenced the drums, and Cao Cao's troops, suspecting an ambush, fell back; then Zhao Yun beat the drums and shot at them with powerful crossbows, and the Cao troops trampled one another and many fell into the Han River and drowned. Liu Bei said Zhao Yun was "courage through and through" (according to the Separate Biography of Zhao Yun). In the 5th month Cao Cao pulled out of Hanzhong.

battle:上庸之战.cmd: Meng Da and Liu Feng vs. Shen Dan
battle:上庸之战.note: Liu Bei sent Meng Da north from Zigui to attack Fangling, where he killed the Administrator Kuai Qi; he also sent his adopted son Liu Feng down the Mian from Hanzhong to take command over Meng Da. Shen Dan, Administrator of Shangyong, surrendered with all his people, and the Three Eastern Commanderies passed to Shu.

battle:樊城之战.cmd: Guan Yu vs. Cao Ren, Yu Jin, Pang De and Xu Huang
battle:樊城之战.note: Guan Yu led his army against Fancheng. In the 8th month there were great rains, the Han River rose several zhang above the plain, and all seven armies under Yu Jin were drowned; Yu Jin surrendered and Pang De, refusing to submit, was beheaded. Bandit bands across the Central Plains accepted seals and titles from Guan Yu from afar, and "his might shook all China"; Cao Cao even considered moving the capital away from Xu to avoid him. Later Xu Huang's relief army broke Guan Yu's siege lines, and with Wu troops striking his rear, Guan Yu lifted the siege and turned south.

battle:白衣渡江.cmd: Lü Meng and Lu Xun vs. Mi Fang and Fu Shiren
battle:白衣渡江.note: Lü Meng pleaded illness and returned to Jianye, and the little-known Lu Xun took over at Lukou to lull Guan Yu. Sun Quan then sent Lü Meng's picked troops hidden in the holds of boats, with the oarsmen dressed in white as merchants; travelling day and night, they captured all the sentries Guan Yu had posted along the river, and Mi Fang, Administrator of Nan Commandery, and Fu Shiren, commanding at Gong'an, surrendered without a fight. After entering Jiangling Lü Meng treated the families of Guan Yu and his officers and men well, and Guan Yu's army lost heart.

battle:麦城之战.cmd: Zhu Ran and Pan Zhang vs. Guan Yu
battle:麦城之战.note: As Guan Yu turned south, his officers and men learned that their families were being well treated by Wu, and many deserted. Guan Yu fell back to hold Maicheng; Sun Quan sent envoys to induce him to surrender, and Guan Yu pretended to agree and slipped away, but at Zhangxiang in Linju he was captured by Ma Zhong, an officer under Pan Zhang, and killed together with his son Guan Ping.

battle:夷陵之战.note: To avenge Guan Yu, Liu Bei led a great army in person down the Yangtze, his camps stretching for several hundred li from the Wu Gorge to Yiling. Lu Xun held his ground and did not come out for seven or eight months; when the Shu army was worn out and weary, he attacked with fire and took more than forty camps at a stroke. Feng Xi, Zhang Nan, Shamoke and others were killed, Du Lu, Liu Ning and others surrendered, and Liu Bei fled through the night back to Baidi City.

battle:洞口之战.mod: on the Yangtze southeast of He County, Anhui
battle:洞口之战.cmd: Cao Xiu, Zhang Liao and Zang Ba vs. Lü Fan, Xu Sheng and Quan Cong
battle:洞口之战.note: Cao Pi attacked Wu along three routes. On the eastern route Cao Xiu brought his army to Dongkou, where Lü Fan led the Wu fleet against him, but a storm sank or scattered the boats and Wu lost several thousand men. Cao Xiu sent Zang Ba on a night attack against Xuling, but he too was driven off by Quan Cong and Xu Sheng; blocked by the Yangtze, Cao Xiu achieved nothing and withdrew.

battle:江陵之战（222）.cmd: Zhu Ran vs. Cao Zhen, Xiahou Shang and Zhang He
battle:江陵之战（222）.note: On the central Wei route Cao Zhen and Xiahou Shang besieged Jiangling. Many in the city were sick and only 5,000 could fight, but Zhu Ran held out for six months, repeatedly sallying out to defeat the Wei troops, and captured and executed Yao Tai, the magistrate of Jiangling, who had plotted to betray the city. The Wei army camped on an island in the river and built a pontoon bridge; Pan Zhang prepared reed rafts to burn it, and on hearing of this Xiahou Shang withdrew his troops. In the 3rd month of the next year the siege was lifted because of an epidemic.

battle:濡须之战（223）.cmd: Zhu Huan vs. Cao Ren and Chang Diao
battle:濡须之战（223）.note: Cao Ren attacked Ruxu with tens of thousands of men, feinting one way and striking another. Zhu Huan had only 5,000 troops, but he sent some of them to meet Chang Diao on the island in the river, beheaded Chang Diao and others, and Cao Ren withdrew.

battle:南中平定.sides: Shu Han defeated the Nanzhong chieftains
battle:南中平定.cmd: Zhuge Liang, Li Hui and Ma Zhong vs. Gao Ding, Yong Kai and Meng Huo
battle:南中平定.note: Zhuge Liang entered Nanzhong from Yuexi and beheaded Gao Ding; Li Hui came out from Pingyi into Yizhou Commandery, and Ma Zhong went into Zangke and put down Zhu Bao. After Yong Kai was killed by Gao Ding's followers, Meng Huo gathered Yong Kai's remaining followers. Zhuge Liang took Ma Su's advice that "winning hearts comes first"; by tradition he captured Meng Huo seven times and released him seven times, until Meng Huo truly submitted and Nanzhong was pacified. Zhuge Liang appointed its chieftains to office, so that the region stayed quiet without garrisons or shipments of grain.

battle:石阳之战.mod: west of Huangpi District, Wuhan, Hubei
battle:石阳之战.note: Just after Cao Pi's death, Sun Quan led 50,000 men in person to besiege Shiyang, seat of Jiangxia Commandery. The Administrator Wen Pin held out; after more than twenty days Sun Quan could not take it, and as he withdrew Wen Pin pursued him. At the same time Zhuge Jin attacked Xiangyang and was defeated by Sima Yi.

battle:新城之战.note: Having received letters from Zhuge Liang, Meng Da plotted to take Xincheng over to Shu, believing that Sima Yi would first have to report to the court and that the round trip would take a month. Sima Yi wrote to reassure Meng Da while marching at double speed, reached the city walls in eight days, and after sixteen days of siege took the city and beheaded Meng Da.

battle:街亭之战.note: On his first northern campaign Zhuge Liang came out by Mount Qi; the three commanderies of Tianshui, Nan'an and Anding rebelled against Wei and went over to him, and Guanzhong was shaken. Against general advice Zhuge Liang put Ma Su in charge of the vanguard; Ma Su disobeyed Zhuge Liang's orders, left the water supply and camped on a hill, and Zhang He cut off his water and routed him. Zhuge Liang withdrew to Hanzhong with more than a thousand households from Xi County, executed Ma Su to atone to the army, and demoted himself three grades. The Romance's "Empty Fort Strategy" is fiction, as Pei Songzhi pointed out long ago.

battle:箕谷之战.cmd: Cao Zhen vs. Zhao Yun and Deng Zhi
battle:箕谷之战.note: Zhuge Liang announced that he would take Mei by the Xie Valley road and sent Zhao Yun and Deng Zhi as a decoy to hold Jigu, pinning down the main army of the Wei General-in-Chief Cao Zhen. Facing a much stronger enemy, Zhao Yun was beaten at Jigu, but he gathered his men and held firm, burning more than a hundred li of plank road north of Chiya, and avoided a serious defeat.

battle:石亭之战.cmd: Lu Xun, Zhu Huan and Quan Cong vs. Cao Xiu
battle:石亭之战.note: Zhou Fang, the Wu Administrator of Poyang, cut off his hair and feigned surrender, luring the Wei Grand Marshal Cao Xiu deep towards Wancheng with 100,000 men. Lu Xun, with Zhu Huan and Quan Cong, attacked from three sides and routed him at Shiting, killing or capturing more than 10,000 and taking 10,000 carts and almost all his supplies and equipment. Cao Xiu escaped thanks to Jia Kui's relief army, but soon fell ill and died.

battle:陈仓之战.mod: east of Chencang District, Baoji, Shaanxi
battle:陈仓之战.note: On his second northern campaign Zhuge Liang came out through San Pass and besieged Chencang. The commander Hao Zhao had only a thousand-odd men. Zhuge Liang attacked in turn with scaling ladders, battering rams, siege towers and tunnels, and Hao Zhao countered each with fire arrows, millstones and a second wall built inside; after more than twenty days of fighting day and night Zhuge Liang ran out of food and withdrew, and the Wei general Wang Shuang, who pursued him, was beheaded.

battle:建威之战.cmd: Zhuge Liang and Chen Shi vs. Guo Huai
battle:建威之战.note: On his third northern campaign Zhuge Liang sent Chen Shi to attack Wudu and Yinping. Guo Huai, Inspector of Yong Province, came to their relief; Zhuge Liang advanced to Jianwei in person, Guo Huai withdrew, and the two commanderies passed to Shu.

battle:子午之役.cmd: Cao Zhen and Sima Yi vs. Zhuge Liang
battle:子午之役.note: Wei attacked Shu by several routes: the Grand Marshal Cao Zhen by the Ziwu Road, the General-in-Chief Sima Yi up the Han River from Xicheng, and another column by the Xie Valley. Zhuge Liang waited at Chenggu and Chiban. It rained for more than thirty days, the plank roads were cut, and the Wei armies turned back halfway.

battle:祁山之战.sides: Minor Shu Han success; withdrew when supplies ran out
battle:祁山之战.cmd: Zhuge Liang vs. Sima Yi and Zhang He
battle:祁山之战.note: On his fourth northern campaign Zhuge Liang brought up grain with "wooden oxen", besieged Mount Qi and sent troops to harvest the wheat of Shanggui. Sima Yi kept behind his walls and refused battle, until, mocked by his officers for "fearing Shu like a tiger", he came out and was beaten by the Shu army. In the 6th month, when Li Yan failed to keep up the grain supply, Zhuge Liang withdrew; Zhang He, pursuing him, was shot and killed on the Mumen Road.

battle:五丈原之战.note: On his fifth northern campaign Zhuge Liang led 100,000 men out through the Xie Valley and camped at the Wuzhang Plains, setting troops to farming as a basis for a long stay. Sima Yi built fortifications with the river at his back and held firm; even when Zhuge Liang sent him a woman's headdress and clothes to provoke him, he did not come out to fight. After more than a hundred days of stalemate, Zhuge Liang died of illness in camp in the 8th month. The Chief Clerk Yang Yi brought the army home in good order; Jiang Wei had the banners turned about and the drums beaten, and Sima Yi dared not press them. People said, "A dead Zhuge put a living Zhongda to flight."

battle:合肥新城之战（234）.note: As agreed with Zhuge Liang, Sun Quan attacked Wei along three routes and besieged Hefei New City in person with 100,000 men. Man Chong recruited several dozen bold men who made torches of pine branches soaked in hemp oil and, with the wind behind them, burned the siege engines; they also shot and killed Sun Quan's nephew Sun Tai. Hearing that Emperor Ming of Wei was marching in person, Sun Quan withdrew.

battle:辽隧之战.note: Emperor Ming of Wei wanted to summon Gongsun Yuan to court and sent Guanqiu Jian, Inspector of You Province, with an army to the southern border of Liaodong. Gongsun Yuan met him at Liaosui; ten days of rain made the Liao River flood, and Guanqiu Jian was beaten and withdrew. Gongsun Yuan then made himself King of Yan.

battle:襄平之战.note: Sima Yi set his timetable as "a hundred days to go, a hundred days to return, a hundred days of fighting, and sixty days of rest". Feinting at Liaosui, he made straight for Xiangping and encircled it after the rains, building earth mounds and digging tunnels and attacking day and night; food ran out in the city and people ate one another. In the 8th month the city fell; Gongsun Yuan and his son were beheaded trying to break out, Sima Yi massacred the city and piled the bodies into a mound, and the four commanderies of Liaodong were pacified.

battle:芍陂之战.mod: south of Shou County, Anhui (Anfeng Pond)
battle:芍陂之战.cmd: Wang Ling and Sun Li vs. Quan Cong
battle:芍陂之战.note: Wu attacked north along four routes. The General of the Guard Quan Cong attacked Huainan, breached Quebei and burned the granaries at Ancheng; the Wei General Who Attacks the East Wang Ling and Sun Li, Inspector of Yang Province, fought hard for several days, Quan Cong withdrew, and the Wu general Qin Huang and others were killed.

battle:樊城之战（241）.note: The Wu General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhu Ran besieged Fancheng. The Grand Tutor Sima Yi asked to lead the relief himself and sent light cavalry to provoke battle; Zhu Ran lifted the siege overnight, and the Wei army pursued him to Sanzhoukou, killing or capturing more than 10,000.

battle:兴势之战.cmd: Wang Ping and Fei Yi vs. Cao Shuang and Xiahou Xuan
battle:兴势之战.note: To make a name for himself, the General-in-Chief Cao Shuang led more than 100,000 foot and horse through the Luo Valley into Hanzhong. Shu had fewer than 30,000 troops in Hanzhong, but Wang Ping first seized the heights of Mount Xingshi and the General-in-Chief Fei Yi followed with reinforcements; the Wei army could not advance, and since supplies from Guanzhong and the Di and Qiang could not keep up and its oxen, horses, mules and donkeys nearly all died, it retreated in disarray, leaving the region west of the passes drained.

battle:丸都之战.cmd: Guanqiu Jian vs. Wigung, King of Goguryeo
battle:丸都之战.note: Guanqiu Jian led 10,000 foot and horse out from Xuantu, routed King Wigung of Goguryeo on the Biryu River, took his capital Hwando and carved an inscription to record his victory (fragments of the "Stele of Guanqiu Jian's Victory" survive). The next year he campaigned again; Wigung fled far away to Okjeo, and the Wei army pursued him to the southern border of the Sushen.

battle:麴城之战.cmd: Guo Huai, Chen Tai and Deng Ai vs. Jiang Wei and Gou An
battle:麴城之战.note: Jiang Wei came out into Longxi and built two forts by Mount Qu, leaving his Gate Generals Gou An and Li Xin to hold them while he joined the Qiang and Hu to press the commanderies. Chen Tai cut their supply route and the stream outside the forts; when Jiang Wei came to the rescue, Guo Huai made for Mount Niutou to cut off his retreat, Jiang Wei withdrew, and Gou An and the others surrendered the forts to Wei.

battle:江陵之战（250）.note: Taking advantage of the unrest in Wu after the dispute between the two palaces, the Wei General Who Attacks the South Wang Chang attacked Jiangling, crossing the water on bridges of bamboo cables. He lured Shi Ji out to fight and routed him, beheading his officers Zhongli Mao and Xu Min.

battle:东兴之战.cmd: Zhuge Ke and Ding Feng vs. Hu Zun and Zhuge Dan
battle:东兴之战.note: Zhuge Ke rebuilt the great Dongxing dyke on the Ruxu River, with a fort on each side against the hills. The Wei generals Hu Zun and Zhuge Dan, with 70,000 men, built pontoon bridges to attack the dyke. It was deep winter and snowing heavily, and the Wei troops were drinking and feasting; Ding Feng led 3,000 men who took off their armour, kept only their helmets, and charged up the dyke with short weapons. The Wei army panicked and scrambled for the crossing, the pontoon bridges broke, and tens of thousands were drowned or killed.

battle:合肥新城之战（253）.cmd: Zhang Te, Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin vs. Zhuge Ke
battle:合肥新城之战（253）.note: After his victory at Dongxing, Zhuge Ke ignored all advice, raised 200,000 men from the provinces and commanderies and besieged Hefei New City. Its Gate General Zhang Te held out for more than ninety days; when the city was about to fall he pretended to ask for terms, used the night to repair the defences, and then refused to surrender. In the summer heat plague broke out in the Wu army and more than half died; Zhuge Ke retreated in disarray and was executed by Sun Jun in the 10th month.

battle:乐嘉之战.sides: Cao Wei defeated Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin
battle:乐嘉之战.cmd: Sima Shi and Deng Ai vs. Wen Qin and Wen Yang
battle:乐嘉之战.note: Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin rose at Shouchun in the name of punishing Sima Shi and advanced to hold Xiang County. Sima Shi took the field in person despite an eye ailment and kept behind his walls. Wen Qin and his son made a night attack on Lejia; the eighteen-year-old Wen Yang led bold men in a noisy assault on the camp, and in his alarm Sima Shi's diseased eye burst from its socket; he bit through his quilt to bear the pain. Wen Qin was beaten and fled south to Wu, and Guanqiu Jian was killed while on the run; Sima Shi died of illness soon after at Xuchang.

battle:洮西之战.cmd: Jiang Wei and Xiahou Ba vs. Wang Jing
battle:洮西之战.note: Jiang Wei and Xiahou Ba came out by Didao. Wang Jing, Inspector of Yong Province, met them at Taoxi and was crushed, losing tens of thousands of men, and fell back to hold the city of Didao. When Chen Tai and Deng Ai came to the rescue, Jiang Wei withdrew to Zhongti. This was the greatest victory of Jiang Wei's northern campaigns.

battle:段谷之战.note: Jiang Wei arranged to meet the General-in-Chief Who Guards the West Hu Ji at Shanggui, but Hu Ji did not arrive in time. Jiang Wei was crushed by Deng Ai at Duangu; his army scattered and many died. The people of Shu blamed him for it, and he petitioned to demote himself to General of the Rear.

battle:寿春之战.sides: Cao Wei defeated Zhuge Dan and Sun Wu
battle:寿春之战.cmd: Sima Zhao vs. Zhuge Dan, Wen Qin and Quan Yi
battle:寿春之战.note: Zhuge Dan rebelled at Shouchun, and Wu sent Wen Qin, Quan Yi and others to help him. Sima Zhao took the emperor and the Empress Dowager with him on campaign; an army of 260,000 surrounded the city on all sides and built long siege lines, and he used double agents to lure Quan Yi and others into surrendering. When food ran out in the city, Zhuge Dan killed Wen Qin. The city fell in the 2nd month of 258; Zhuge Dan was beheaded trying to break out, and several hundred of his men submitted to execution without resistance, all saying "To die for Lord Zhuge, we have no regrets."

battle:阳安关之战.cmd: Hu Lie (Zhong Hui's army) vs. Fu Qian and Jiang Shu
battle:阳安关之战.note: Zhong Hui sent the Army Protector Hu Lie ahead to attack the pass (Yang'an Pass). The Shu commander Jiang Shu opened the gates and surrendered, his deputy Fu Qian died fighting, and Zhong Hui drove straight into Hanzhong, capturing large stores of grain.

battle:剑阁之战.cmd: Jiang Wei, Liao Hua and Zhang Yi vs. Zhong Hui
battle:剑阁之战.note: Hearing that Hanzhong was lost, Jiang Wei broke away from Tazhong, shaking off Deng Ai and Zhuge Xu, joined forces with Liao Hua, Zhang Yi and Dong Jue and fell back to hold Jiange. Camped in the narrows, they held off Zhong Hui's army of more than 100,000; with supplies hard to bring up, Zhong Hui even considered withdrawing.

battle:绵竹之战.cmd: Deng Ai vs. Zhuge Zhan, Zhuge Shang and Huang Chong
battle:绵竹之战.note: Deng Ai came out at Jiangyou, and the Shu General of the Guard Zhuge Zhan fell back from Fu to hold Mianzhu. Deng Ai tried to tempt him with the title King of Langya, and Zhuge Zhan angrily beheaded the envoy. Deng Ai sent his son Deng Zhong and Shi Zuan to attack on the two wings; they were beaten at first, and when Deng Ai threatened to behead them they attacked again and routed the Shu army. Zhuge Zhan and his son, Huang Chong, Zhang Zun and others all died fighting, and the way to Chengdu lay open.

battle:万斛堆之战.note: Tufa Shujineng of the Hexi Xianbei rose against Jin. Hu Lie, Inspector of Qin Province, led an army against him and was surrounded at Wanhudui, defeated and killed. Shujineng went on raiding year after year, and in 279 even took Liang Province for a time.

battle:交趾之战.cmd: Tao Huang, Yu Si and Xue Xu vs. Yang Ji and Mao Jiong
battle:交趾之战.note: From 268 Wu repeatedly sent large armies to contest Jiao Province. In 271 Tao Huang and others besieged Jiaozhi; when food ran out in the city, Yang Ji, the Administrator appointed by Jin, the general Mao Jiong and others surrendered; Jiuzhen and Rinan followed and returned to Wu, and Tao Huang was made Inspector of Jiao Province.

battle:西陵之战.sides: Sun Wu defeated Jin and Bu Chan
battle:西陵之战.cmd: Lu Kang vs. Bu Chan, Yang Zhao and Yang Hu
battle:西陵之战.note: Bu Chan, the Wu commander at Xiling, surrendered his city to Jin. Lu Kang had his troops build strong siege lines around Xiling, both to stop Bu Chan breaking out and to hold off Jin relief, and broke the dams near Jiangling to hinder Yang Hu's water transport. In the 12th month he drove off Yang Zhao, Inspector of Jing Province, Yang Hu also withdrew, and Lu Kang took Xiling and executed Bu Chan and several dozen fellow conspirators.

battle:武威之战.note: Ma Long, Army Protector Who Punishes the Caitiffs, recruited 3,500 brave men for a western campaign. Following the Eight-Formation Diagram he built carts with side screens: in open country they formed a camp ringed with deer-horn abatis, and on narrow roads wooden shelters were mounted on the carts. Fighting his way across a thousand li, he beheaded Shujineng and pacified Liang Province.

battle:西陵荆门之战.mod: the Yangtze from Yichang to Yidu, Hubei
battle:西陵荆门之战.cmd: Wang Jun and Tang Bin vs. Liu Xian, Lu Yan and Lu Jing
battle:西陵荆门之战.note: Wu had stretched iron chains across the narrows of the Yangtze and sunk iron spikes more than a zhang long in the river. Wang Jun first sent dozens of great rafts carrying armoured straw men downstream to carry off the spikes, then made torches more than ten zhang long and dozens of arm-spans round, soaked in hemp oil, to melt the chains, so that his tower ships sailed down unhindered and took Xiling, Jingmen, Yidao and Lexiang in succession.

battle:江陵之战（280）.note: Du Yu, General-in-Chief Who Guards the South, attacked Jiangling; he sent a surprise force across to the south bank by night to spread word that the main army had arrived, and the Wu commander Sun Xin was captured. In the 2nd month he took Jiangling and beheaded the Wu commander Wu Yan, and the provinces and commanderies south of the Yuan and Xiang went over at the news. Du Yu said, "Our arms are now in full force; it is like splitting bamboo," and urged pressing on straight to Jianye.

battle:版桥之战.mod: area northeast of He County, Anhui (location disputed)
battle:版桥之战.cmd: Wang Hun and Zhang Qiao vs. Zhang Ti, Shen Ying and Sun Zhen
battle:版桥之战.note: The Wu Chancellor Zhang Ti, with Shen Ying, Administrator of Danyang, and 30,000 men, crossed the Yangtze to meet Wang Hun. He first forced Zhang Qiao to surrender, then attacked Wang Hun's main body; Shen Ying's picked Danyang troops charged three times without breaking the Jin line, then fell into disorder and broke. Zhang Ti refused Zhuge Jing's urging to flee and died fighting, and the main Wu army fell apart.

pass:函谷关.mod: east of Xin'an, Henan (Han Hangu Pass site)
pass:函谷关.note: Under Emperor Wu of Han it was moved east from Hongnong to Xin'an, as the western gateway to Luoyang; the old pass is at today's Lingbao.

pass:潼关.note: At the end of the Eastern Han a pass was set up at the bend of the Yellow River, and the line between "west of the passes" and "east of the passes" moved west to here. In 211 Cao Cao faced Ma Chao and Han Sui here.

pass:武关.note: The southeastern gateway of Guanzhong, leading to Nanyang and Jing–Xiang.

pass:散关.note: Northern entrance of the Chencang Road (Gudao Road). Cao Cao went this way against Zhang Lu in 215, and Zhuge Liang came out this way to besiege Chencang in winter 228.

pass:陇关.note: The pass at the eastern foot of the Long Mountains, on the main road from Guanzhong to Longyou.

pass:萧关.note: The gateway from Guanzhong to Anding and Beidi.

pass:阳平关.mod: west of Mian County, Shaanxi (the Han-era Yangping Pass)
pass:阳平关.note: The western gateway of Hanzhong, also called Yang'an Pass. Cao Cao broke Zhang Wei here in 215, Liu Bei faced Xiahou Yuan here from 217 to 219, and in 263 Zhong Hui sent Hu Lie to take the pass.

pass:白水关.note: The key pass on the northern edge of Yi Province, held for Liu Zhang by Yang Huai and Gao Pei; in 212 Liu Bei beheaded the two commanders, took the pass and marched south.

pass:剑阁.note: Where the cliffs of Mount Dajian break, Zhuge Liang cut into the rock to build a suspended plank road, posting a Gallery Commandant to guard it. In 263 Jiang Wei held it against Zhong Hui's great army.

pass:江油.note: The southern end of the Yinping Road. In 263 Deng Ai's surprise force reached here, and the commander holding it, Ma Miao, surrendered.

pass:沓中.note: From 262 Jiang Wei set up military farms here to stay out of trouble at court; in 263 he was pinned down by Deng Ai and could not return in time to relieve Hanzhong.

pass:祁山.mod: east of Li County, Gansu (Qishan Fort)
pass:祁山.note: A lone peak on the north bank of the Xihan River, guarding the main route from Longyou to Hanzhong. Zhuge Liang came out by Mount Qi on his first and fourth northern campaigns; the Romance stretches this into "six sorties from Mount Qi".

pass:虎牢关.note: That is, Chenggao Pass, the eastern gateway of Luoyang; Xuanmen Pass to its west was one of the Eight Passes of Luoyang in the late Han. The Romance sets "the three heroes fight Lü Bu" here, but in the histories the coalition against Dong Zhuo never fought Lü Bu here.

pass:伊阙关.note: The southern gateway of Luoyang, one of the Eight Passes of Luoyang in the late Han.

pass:轘辕关.mod: southeast of Yanshi District, Luoyang, Henan
pass:轘辕关.note: The route southeast from Luoyang past Mount Songgao to Yingchuan, one of the Eight Passes of Luoyang in the late Han.

pass:孟津.mod: northeast of Mengjin District, Luoyang, Henan
pass:孟津.note: The Yellow River crossing north of Luoyang, including Xiaoping Ford, one of the Eight Passes of Luoyang in the late Han. In 189 Zhang Rang and the other eunuchs abducted the Young Emperor and fled here, then drowned themselves in the river.

pass:壶关.note: The western end of a defile through the Taihang Mountains and the eastern gateway of Shangdang. In 206 Gao Gan held it against Cao Cao.

pass:井陉.mod: west of Luquan District, Shijiazhuang, Hebei (Tumen Pass)
pass:井陉.note: One of the Eight Defiles of the Taihang, the main route from Hebei to Bing Province.

pass:句注.mod: northwest of Dai County, Shanxi (Yanmen Pass area)
pass:句注.note: The northern gate of Bing Province, also called the Western Defile.

pass:居庸关.note: A key pass in the western Yan Mountains.

pass:卢龙塞.note: A pass in the eastern Yan Mountains, from which one could go beyond the frontier straight to Liucheng. In 207 Cao Cao followed Tian Chou's plan and made his surprise attack on the Wuhuan this way.

pass:玉门关.note: The Han pass on the Northern Route of the Western Regions.

pass:阳关.note: The Han pass on the Southern Route of the Western Regions.

pass:濡须坞.note: In 212, on Lü Meng's advice, Sun Quan built this fort astride the mouth of the Ruxu River, shaped like a crescent moon; afterwards Cao Cao and Cao Ren attacked it again and again without taking it, and it was Wu's foremost stronghold north of the Yangtze.

pass:合肥新城.note: In 230 Man Chong, judging that the old city was too close to the water and exposed to the Wu fleet, built a new city thirty li to its northwest; the great Wu sieges of 234 and 253 both failed to take it.

pass:牛渚.note: One of the most important crossings on the lower Yangtze; Sun Ce crossed the river here in 194–195.

pass:荆门·虎牙.note: The gateway of the Yangtze as it leaves the Three Gorges, with Mount Jingmen on the south bank and Mount Huya on the north. Wu stretched iron chains across the river here, which Wang Jun burned through in 280.

event:燕然勒铭.note: After routing the Northern Xiongnu, Dou Xian climbed the Yanran Mountains and had the Army Protector of the Centre Ban Gu compose an inscription carved in the rock, "performing the feng rite on the mountain and cutting the stone to proclaim supreme virtue". In 2017 a joint Chinese–Mongolian survey team found and deciphered this cliff inscription in Dundgovi Province, Mongolia.

event:蔡伦造纸.note: Cai Lun, Regular Palace Attendant and Director of the Imperial Workshops, made paper from tree bark, hemp ends, rags and old fishing nets and presented it in 105; "from then on everyone used it, and the whole realm called it Marquis Cai's paper".

event:张衡地动仪.note: Zhang Heng, Grand Astrologer, made a seismoscope cast in fine bronze, shaped like a wine vessel, with a dragon's mouth holding a ball in each of the eight directions; in 138 it detected an earthquake in Longxi.

event:党锢之祸.note: Under Emperors Huan and Ling the eunuchs twice launched great purges: more than a hundred men, including Li Ying, Du Mi and Fan Pang, died in prison, and six or seven hundred partisans across the country were barred from office, turning the scholar class against the court. The partisans were only pardoned when the Yellow Turbans rose in 184.

event:熹平石经.mod: Yanshi, Luoyang, Henan (Imperial Academy site, Han–Wei Luoyang city)
event:熹平石经.note: Cai Yong and others petitioned to fix the texts of the Confucian classics, which were carved in clerical script on forty-six stelae set up outside the gate of the Imperial Academy in Luoyang; more than a thousand carriages a day came to view and copy them.

event:黄巾起事.note: Zhang Jue called himself the "General of Heaven" and his brothers Zhang Bao and Zhang Liang the Generals "of Earth" and "of Man". Under the slogan "The Blue Heaven is dead, the Yellow Heaven shall rise; in the year jiazi the world will have great fortune", the thirty-six divisions rose on the same day, burning government offices and plundering towns, and within a month the whole realm responded.

event:十常侍之乱.note: He Jin entered the palace to ask for the eunuchs to be executed and was beheaded in front of the Jiade Hall by Zhang Rang, Duan Gui and others. Yuan Shao and Yuan Shu led troops into the palace and killed every eunuch, more than 2,000 in all; Zhang Rang and the others abducted the Young Emperor and the King of Chenliu and fled by night to Xiaoping Ford, where they drowned themselves in the river. Dong Zhuo met the emperor at Beimang with his army and so took control of the court.

event:酸枣会盟.note: The armies east of the passes made Yuan Shao leader of the alliance. Zang Hong mounted the altar, smeared his lips with blood and swore the oath, his words so stirring that all who heard were roused. But the armies feared Dong Zhuo's strength and feasted every day without trying to advance; Cao Cao rebuked them to no effect, and in the end they ran out of food and dispersed.

event:焚洛阳迁长安.old: Luoyang burned, court moved to Chang'an
event:焚洛阳迁长安.note: Dong Zhuo forced Emperor Xian to move west to Chang'an and drove several million people of Luoyang along with him; harried by foot and horse, they trampled one another and the road was strewn with corpses. He also set fire to the palaces, temples, offices and homes, so that every building within two hundred li was destroyed, and dug up the imperial tombs and the graves of high officials for their treasures.

event:孙坚入洛.note: Sun Jian defeated Dong Zhuo's army and entered Luoyang; he cleaned the Han ancestral temples, offered the full sacrifice and repaired the tombs that had been dug up. The Book of Wu says Sun Jian found the Han imperial seal in the Zhenguan well south of the city, but this story is doubtful.

event:王允诛董卓.mod: northwest of Xi'an, Shaanxi (Han Chang'an city site)
event:王允诛董卓.note: The Minister over the Masses Wang Yun plotted with Dong Zhuo's adopted son Lü Bu. When the officials gathered to celebrate Emperor Xian's recovery from illness, Lü Bu killed Dong Zhuo with his own hands at the northern side gate of the Weiyang Palace, and the officials and people of Chang'an celebrated. Dong Zhuo's corpse was set alight and its fat ran over the ground; the 20,000–30,000 jin of gold and 80,000–90,000 jin of silver stored in Mei Fort were all confiscated.

event:献帝东归.note: Li Jue and Guo Si fought each other and Chang'an lay in ruins. In the 7th month of 195 Emperor Xian set out east, pursued all the way by Li Jue and Guo Si, and almost all his officials were killed or wounded. He reached Luoyang in the 7th month of 196 to find the palaces burned to the ground; the officials pushed through brambles to shelter among the ruined walls, and those below the rank of Gentleman of the Secretariat went out themselves to gather wild grain.

event:迁都许县.note: Taking Mao Jie's advice to "serve the Son of Heaven to command those who do not submit" and Xun Yu's to "serve the sovereign to follow the people's hopes", Cao Cao went to Luoyang to receive Emperor Xian and moved him to Xu. He made himself Excellency of Works and acting General of Chariots and Cavalry, the officials all took orders from him, and he gained the political initiative.

event:许下屯田.note: On the advice of Zao Zhi and Han Hao, Cao Cao recruited people to farm around Xu as military farms, harvesting a million hu of grain in the first year. Farm officials were later set up in every province and commandery, so that "campaigns in all directions needed no grain transport", laying the material foundation for unifying the north.

event:袁术称帝.note: Taking the prophecy "He who replaces the Han shall be the high one on the road" to refer to himself, Yuan Shu proclaimed himself emperor at Shouchun with the dynastic name Zhong, appointed ministers and sacrificed at the southern and northern altars. He lived in debauched luxury, with several hundred palace women all dressed in fine silk, while his soldiers froze and starved and the people between the Yangtze and the Huai ate one another until almost none were left.

event:煮酒论英雄.note: While Liu Bei was serving Cao Cao, Cao Cao said to him casually, "The only heroes in the realm today are you and I; the likes of Benchu don't count". Liu Bei, who was eating, dropped his spoon and chopsticks in alarm. Soon afterwards he left Xu, using the mission to intercept Yuan Shu. The scene of "green plums and warmed wine" was added by the Romance.

event:衣带诏.note: The General of Chariots and Cavalry Dong Cheng claimed to have received a secret edict from Emperor Xian hidden in a girdle, and plotted with Liu Bei, Chong Ji, Wu Zilan, Wang Fu and others to kill Cao Cao. The plot was discovered; Dong Cheng and the others were executed along with the three branches of their families, and even the pregnant Consort Dong was killed. Liu Bei had already left to take charge of Xu Province and escaped.

event:孙策遇刺.note: Sun Ce planned to strike at Xu while the Guandu campaign was under way, but while out hunting he was attacked by retainers of Xu Gong, the former Administrator of Wu Commandery. Mortally wounded, he entrusted his brother Sun Quan to Zhang Zhao, telling Sun Quan, "In raising the worthy and employing the able so that each gives his all to protect Jiangdong, I am not your equal". He was only twenty-six.

event:伤寒杂病论.old: Treatise on Cold Damage and Miscellaneous Diseases
event:伤寒杂病论.note: Zhang Zhongjing of Nanyang, moved by the death within ten years of two-thirds of his clan of more than two hundred people, seven in ten of them from cold-damage disorders, "diligently sought the ancient teachings and gathered prescriptions widely" and wrote the Treatise on Cold Damage and Miscellaneous Diseases in sixteen juan. It established the principle of treatment based on pattern differentiation, and later ages honoured him as the "Sage of Medicine".

event:隆中对.note: When Liu Bei called on Zhuge Liang three times at Longzhong, Zhuge Liang analysed the state of the realm for him: concede the timing of Heaven to Cao Cao in the north and the advantage of terrain to Sun Quan in the east; take Jing and Yi provinces first, make peace with the Rong tribes to the west and pacify the Yi and Yue to the south, ally with Sun Quan abroad and put government in order at home; then, when the realm changes, attack north along two routes, and hegemony can be won.

event:华容道.note: After the defeat at Red Cliffs Cao Cao led the remnants of his army north on foot along the Huarong Road.
