The road was deep in mud and impassable, and a strong wind was blowing, so he ordered his weaker soldiers to carry grass to fill in the road so that the cavalry could pass; the weak soldiers were trampled into the mud by men and horses, and many died. The Romance's story of Guan Yu releasing Cao Cao at Huarong out of loyalty is fiction.

event:刘备取荆南.old: Liu Bei takes southern Jing Province
event:刘备取荆南.note: After Red Cliffs Liu Bei marched south against Wuling, Changsha, Guiyang and Lingling; the four Administrators, Jin Xuan, Han Xuan, Zhao Fan and Liu Du, all surrendered, and Huang Zhong joined Liu Bei at this time. In the Romance, Zhao Yun's capture of Guiyang, Guan Yu's duel with Huang Zhong and similar episodes are mostly fiction.

event:铜雀台.mod: southwest of Linzhang, Hebei (Ye city site)
event:铜雀台.note: Cao Cao built the Bronze Sparrow Terrace northwest of Ye, which with the Golden Tiger and Ice Well terraces formed the Three Terraces; in the same year he issued his Edict Seeking the Worthy, calling for men "chosen for talent alone". Cao Cao and his sons gathered at Ye with the Seven Masters of the Jian'an era and others, "passionate and spirited, bold and open in their talent", forming the literature of the Jian'an era.

event:孙权徙治秣陵.old: Sun Quan moves his seat to Moling
event:孙权徙治秣陵.note: On Zhang Hong's advice Sun Quan moved his seat from Jingkou to Moling; in 212 he built Stone City on Mount Qingliang and renamed Moling as Jianye, meaning "establishing the great enterprise of emperors and kings". After proclaiming himself emperor in 229 he made it his capital.

event:曹操称魏公.old: Cao Cao made Duke of Wei
event:曹操称魏公.mod: southwest of Linzhang, Hebei (Ye city site)
event:曹操称魏公.note: Emperor Xian enfeoffed Cao Cao as Duke of Wei with the Nine Bestowments, making ten commanderies of Ji Province into the state of Wei with Ye as its capital and a full government from Chancellor down. In 216 he was raised to King of Wei, and the next year he was granted the emperor's banners; the stage was set for the Cao family to replace the Han.

event:单刀会.note: When Sun Quan could not get Jing Province back, he sent Lü Meng to seize Changsha, Lingling and Guiyang, and Lu Su camped at Yiyang to hold off Guan Yu. Lu Su invited Guan Yu to a meeting: each side kept its troops a hundred paces away, and the generals met "each with a single blade", while Lu Su took Guan Yu to task. The Romance has Guan Yu going to the meeting alone with his blade and leaving at his ease, reversing host and guest.

event:湘水划界.note: Hearing that Cao Cao had entered Hanzhong, Liu Bei feared losing Yi Province and made peace with Sun Quan, dividing Jing Province along the Xiang River: Changsha, Jiangxia and Guiyang in the east went to Sun Quan, and Nan Commandery, Lingling and Wuling in the west to Liu Bei.

event:南匈奴分五部.old: Southern Xiongnu split into Five Divisions
event:南匈奴分五部.note: Cao Cao kept the Southern Chanyu Huchuquan at Ye and sent the Worthy King of the Right Qubei to oversee his people, dividing them into five divisions, Left, Right, South, North and Centre, each led by one of their nobles and supervised by a Han Chinese Major, and settling them across the commanderies of Bing Province. At the end of the Western Jin Liu Yuan raised his rebellion with the Five Divisions of the Xiongnu.

event:曹丕受禅.note: Emperor Xian of Han abdicated to Cao Pi, King of Wei, who built the Abdication Terrace at Fanyang Pavilion, took the throne and changed the era to Huangchu. Emperor Xian was made Duke of Shanyang and lived until 234. The Abdication Terrace and two stelae, the Record of the Abdication and the Memorial of the Ministers and Generals Urging the Title, survive at Linying in Henan.

event:九品中正制.note: Cao Pi, King of Wei, adopted the proposal of Chen Qun of the Secretariat to appoint Rectifiers in each province and commandery, who graded the gentry into nine ranks by family background, talent and virtue for the Ministry of Personnel to select officials. It lasted nearly four hundred years and gradually became a tool by which great families monopolised office.

event:刘备称帝.note: On rumours that Emperor Xian had been murdered, Liu Bei took the imperial throne south of Mount Wudan in Chengdu, with the dynastic name Han and the era name Zhangwu, and made Zhuge Liang Chancellor. Because he held the land of Shu, historians call his state "Shu Han" or "Shu".

event:孙权受封吴王.old: Sun Quan made King of Wu
event:孙权受封吴王.note: Sun Quan moved his capital from Gong'an to E County and renamed it Wuchang. In the 8th month he sent envoys to declare himself a vassal of Wei, and Cao Pi made him King of Wu with the Nine Bestowments. Sun Quan used this to secure his northern front and concentrate on holding off Liu Bei in the west; after his victory at Yiling he broke with Wei.

event:白帝托孤.note: Gravely ill, Liu Bei summoned Zhuge Liang from Chengdu and entrusted his affairs to him: "Your talent is ten times that of Cao Pi; you will surely bring peace to the state and accomplish the great task. If my heir can be helped, help him; if he is unfit, you may take the throne yourself." Zhuge Liang wept and swore to serve with all his strength and unswerving loyalty until death.

event:吴蜀复盟.note: Zhuge Liang sent Deng Zhi of the Secretariat as envoy to Sun Quan. Deng Zhi argued that Wu and Shu depended on each other like lips and teeth, and Sun Quan broke off relations with Wei and allied with Shu alone; the two states never fought each other again.

event:曹丕临江.note: Cao Pi personally led more than 100,000 men in a fleet to the old city of Guangling and reviewed his troops on the Yangtze, his banners stretching for several hundred li. It was so cold that the waterways were frozen and the ships could not get into the river; seeing the surging waves, Cao Pi sighed "Alas! Heaven surely set this here to divide north from south" and led his army back north.

event:出师表.note: As Zhuge Liang led the armies north to Hanzhong, he submitted a memorial before setting out, recalling the late emperor's three visits and his charge on his deathbed, urging Liu Shan to keep worthy men close and flatterers away, and declaring that he would "lead the three armies north to pacify the Central Plains, exert my poor abilities to the full, remove the treacherous and evil, restore the house of Han and return to the old capital". He was then based at Mianyang for nearly eight years.

event:孙权称帝.note: Sun Quan took the imperial throne in the southern suburbs of Wuchang, changed the era to Huanglong, and in the 9th month moved his capital to Jianye. Shu Han allied with Wu on the basis of "honouring both emperors", agreeing to divide the realm once Wei was destroyed.

event:卫温航海夷洲.note: Sun Quan sent the generals Wei Wen and Zhuge Zhi with 10,000 armoured troops across the sea in search of Yizhou and Danzhou; they brought back several thousand people from Yizhou, but eight or nine in ten of the soldiers died of disease, and the two generals were imprisoned and executed for disobeying orders and achieving nothing. Yizhou is generally thought to be today's Taiwan.

event:倭女王遣使.mod: Sariwon area, North Hwanghae, North Korea
event:倭女王遣使.note: Himiko, queen of Wa, sent the official Nashime and others through Daifang Commandery to Luoyang with tribute; Emperor Ming of Wei named Himiko "King of Wa, Friend of Wei", granted her a gold seal with a purple ribbon and gave her a hundred bronze mirrors. The section on the Wa in the Account of the Eastern Peoples in the Records of the Three Kingdoms is one of the most important sources for early Japanese history.

event:正始玄学.note: He Yan, Wang Bi and others interpreted the Book of Changes and the Analects through the teachings of Laozi and Zhuangzi, exalting "non-being" and opening the Wei–Jin fashion for pure conversation and Xuanxue ("Dark Learning"). Wang Bi died at twenty-four, leaving commentaries on the Laozi and the Book of Changes. After the Incident at the Gaoping Tombs He Yan was killed, and the scholarly fashion shifted to the Bamboo Grove.

event:高平陵之变.mod: south of Luoyang, Henan (northern foot of Mount Wan'an)
event:高平陵之变.note: While the General-in-Chief Cao Shuang and his brothers accompanied the young emperor Cao Fang to pay respects at Emperor Ming's Gaoping Tomb, the Grand Tutor Sima Yi, on the authority of the Empress Dowager, shut the gates of Luoyang, posted troops at the pontoon bridge on the Luo River and petitioned for the dismissal of Cao Shuang and his brothers. Cao Shuang rejected Huan Fan's advice to take the emperor to Xuchang, returned to Luoyang and gave up his command; a few days later he was executed for treason and the three branches of his family wiped out, and He Yan, Ding Mi, Deng Yang and others were drawn in.

event:竹林之游.note: Ji Kang, Ruan Ji, Shan Tao, Xiang Xiu, Liu Ling, Wang Rong and Ruan Xian often gathered in a bamboo grove in Shanyang County to drink freely and without restraint, and were known as the "Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove"; under the Sima dictatorship many of them used unconventional behaviour to stay out of danger. Around 262 Ji Kang was put to death by Sima Zhao, playing the tune Guangling San before his execution.

event:曹髦之死.note: The Wei emperor Cao Mao, unable to bear Sima Zhao's domination, exclaimed angrily, "Sima Zhao's heart is known to every passer-by", and personally led several hundred palace servants against him. Cheng Ji, a Retainer of the Heir, on the orders of the Army Protector of the Centre Jia Chong, stabbed him to death beneath his carriage. He was twenty.

event:邓艾偷渡阴平.old: Deng Ai's covert march through Yinping
event:邓艾偷渡阴平.mod: between Qingchuan, Sichuan and Wen County, Gansu (Motian Ridge)
event:邓艾偷渡阴平.note: Deng Ai took the Yinping Road through more than 700 li of uninhabited country, cutting through mountains and building bridges and galleries. The mountains were high and the valleys deep, and food was running out; Deng Ai wrapped himself in felt and rolled down the slopes, while his officers and men climbed along trees and cliffs in single file. They surprised Jiangyou, and the commander holding it, Ma Miao, surrendered.

event:刘禅出降.note: When Deng Ai's army reached Chengdu, the Grandee of the Palace Qiao Zhou argued strongly for surrender. Liu Shan bound himself, brought his own coffin and surrendered at Deng Ai's camp gate, and Shu Han fell; Liu Chen, King of Beidi, wept at the temple of Emperor Zhaolie and killed himself. Liu Shan was moved to Luoyang and made Duke of Anle, leaving the saying "I am happy here and do not miss Shu".

event:钟会之乱.note: Zhong Hui falsely accused Deng Ai of rebellion and had him taken back in a cage cart, then plotted with the surrendered general Jiang Wei to hold Shu for himself, intending to kill all the generals who had come from the north. The plot leaked, the generals' men mutinied, and Zhong Hui and Jiang Wei were both killed; Deng Ai was also killed while being escorted away.

event:晋代魏.note: After Sima Zhao's death his son Sima Yan succeeded him as King of Jin; four months later Cao Huan, Emperor Yuan of Wei, abdicated, and Sima Yan took the throne in the southern suburbs of Luoyang, naming his state Jin and changing the era to Taishi. Early Jin made twenty-seven members of the imperial clan kings, sowing the seeds of the later War of the Eight Kings.

event:裴秀制图.note: Pei Xiu, the Western Jin Excellency of Works, directed the compilation of the Regional Maps of the Tribute of Yu in eighteen sheets. In its preface he set out six principles of mapmaking: graduated scale, rectangular grid, measured distances, levelling of heights, measurement of angles, and straightening of curves; these laid the foundations of traditional Chinese cartography.

event:王濬造楼船.note: Emperor Wu of Jin secretly ordered Wang Jun, Inspector of Yi Province, to build a great fleet in Shu. The largest, made of lashed hulls, were 120 paces square and could carry more than 2,000 men, with towers and gates on four sides and room for horses to gallop on deck. Wood shavings from the shipyards floated down the Yangtze; Wu Yan, the Wu Administrator of Jianping, collected them and reported them to the court, but Sun Hao paid no attention.

event:孙皓降晋.note: Wang Jun's tower ships sailed straight to Stone City, and Sun Hao, ruler of Wu, came out to surrender in a plain carriage drawn by a white horse, stripped to the waist with his hands tied, holding a jade disc in his mouth and leading a sheep; Wu was no more. This ended nearly a century of division that had begun with the Yellow Turbans in 184, and Jin gained Wu's four provinces, forty-three commanderies and 523,000 households.

people:南匈奴.note: They submitted to the Han in 48; the Chanyu's court was at Meiji in Xihe.

people:匈奴五部.note: In 216 Cao Cao divided the Southern Xiongnu into five divisions settled across the commanderies of Bing Province.

people:乌桓.note: Under the Eastern Han they moved into the frontier commanderies of Shanggu, Yuyang, Youbeiping, Liaoxi and Liaodong, and a Colonel Protector of the Wuhuan was stationed at Ningcheng in Shanggu.

people:轲比能部.note: A minor Xianbei group that became the strongest in the late Han and Three Kingdoms, raiding You and Bing provinces repeatedly; in 235 Wang Xiong, the Wei Inspector of You Province, had Kebineng assassinated.

people:拓跋鲜卑.note: In 258 Tuoba Liwei moved to Shengle in Dingxiang; his descendants founded the Northern Wei.

people:慕容鲜卑.note: Mohuba won merit following Sima Yi against Gongsun Yuan, was made King Who Leads in Righteousness, and settled north of Jicheng.

people:秃发鲜卑.note: They lived in Hexi. From 270 to 279 Tufa Shujineng rebelled against Jin and threw Liang Province into turmoil.

people:小月氏（湟中胡）.note: Remnants of the Yuezhi who stayed behind in Huangzhong when the Yuezhi moved west; under the Eastern Han they were called the Huangzhong Auxiliary Hu, and in 184 they joined the Liang Province rebellion.

people:氐.note: They lived around Wudu and Yinping; in the late Han there were Di kings such as Qianwan and A Gui, and both Wei and Shu sought their support.

people:賨人（板楯蛮）.note: They lived around Dangqu in Ba Commandery and were famed as brave, fierce fighters.

people:南中夷（叟、濮）.note: The peoples of the seven commanderies of Nanzhong; after his southern campaign Zhuge Liang formed their best fighters into the "Flying Army".

people:武陵蛮（五溪蛮）.note: At the Battle of Yiling in 222 Shamoke, chief of the Wuxi tribes, led his people to help Liu Bei and was killed.

people:山越.note: Descendants of the Yue scattered through the hills of Danyang, Kuaiji and Yuzhang. Sun Wu campaigned against them many times; Zhuge Ke subdued the Shanyue of Danyang in 234–237 and gained 40,000 armoured troops.

people:乌浒·俚.note: Native peoples of the Yulin and Hepu area of Jiao Province.

people:黎（儋耳·珠崖）.note: Hainan Island had been outside the commandery system since Emperor Yuan of the Western Han abolished Zhuya Commandery; in 242 Wu sent Nie You and Lu Kai to conquer it and re-established Zhuya Commandery.

people:夷洲.note: Generally thought to be today's Taiwan. In 230 Sun Quan sent Wei Wen and Zhuge Zhi across the sea, and they reached it.

people:倭.note: The Account of the Eastern Peoples in the Records of the Three Kingdoms says the Wa once had more than a hundred states, of which thirty now had dealings through envoys and interpreters; the queen Himiko had her capital in the state of Yamatai.

people:沃沮.note: In 245 Guanqiu Jian pursued the king of Goguryeo as far as here.

people:乌孙.note: Its capital was Chigu City; a great state of the Western Regions in Han times.

battle:下辨之战.sides: Cao Cao (Cao Hong) defeated Liu Bei (Wu Lan)
battle:下辨之战.cmd: Cao Hong and Cao Xiu vs. Wu Lan and Zhang Fei
battle:下辨之战.note: Liu Bei sent Zhang Fei, Ma Chao and Wu Lan to camp at Xiabian, and Zhang Fei let it be known that he would cut off the enemy's retreat. Cao Xiu saw through this and urged Cao Hong to strike Wu Lan at once; they routed him and beheaded his officer Ren Kui. Zhang Fei and Ma Chao withdrew, and Wu Lan fled to Yinping, where the Di killed him.
